Northside Code Co-op
  • What you'll learn
  • Schedule
  • Register
  • FAQ
Reserve a seat
Saturday · 10:00 AM · In-person + Zoom

Learn Git in one focused Saturday.

A hands-on, from-zero intro to version control. Bring a laptop; leave with your first repo pushed, a working branching model, and the confidence to collaborate without breaking things.

Reserve a seat — free See the schedule
Date · Sat, Oct 4
Time · 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM
Where · 512 Boylston, Rm 304
Cost · Free (donation optional)

No prior Git needed

We assume you've opened a terminal once. That's it.

Bring your own project

The last hour is for putting your own code under version control, with help.

Small group

Capped at 24 seats so questions actually get answered.

What you'll walk out knowing

By the end of the day you'll have a working mental model of Git — not just a list of commands you copy-pasted once.

01

The commit as a snapshot

Why Git thinks in snapshots, not diffs — and why that changes how you work.

02

Branch, merge, rebase

When each is the right tool, plus how to get out of the ones you regret.

03

Remotes & GitHub

Push, pull, PRs, and the etiquette of collaborating without stepping on toes.

04

Recovering from mistakes

reflog, reset, revert — the safety net that lets you experiment.

05

A workflow you can keep

A simple branching model that scales from solo projects to small teams.

06

Your own repo, pushed

Leave with a real project on GitHub, README and all.

The day, hour by hour

Short lessons, lots of practice. We take a real lunch break.

10:00
Setup & welcomeInstall check, terminal warmup, why version control at all.
10:30
Your first commitinit, add, commit — and what actually happened on disk.
11:30
Branching without fearFeature branches, switching, merging clean and messy.
12:30
Lunch (provided)Sandwiches, coffee, informal Q&A.
13:15
GitHub & pull requestsRemotes, forks, PR review flow.
14:15
Bring-your-own-project labGet your own code under Git with a mentor.
15:00
Wrap & next stepsCheat sheet, further reading, community office hours.

Reserve your seat

The workshop is free thanks to our sponsors. We cap it at 24 seats so everyone gets real one-on-one time. Cancellations open a spot for the waitlist.

✓ Free✓ Lunch included✓ Beginners welcome

Common questions

If yours isn't here, email hi@northsidecodecoop.org.

Do I need to know how to code?

Not really — if you can save a text file and open a terminal, you're set.

What laptop should I bring?

Mac, Windows, or Linux — all work. We'll help you install Git if you haven't.

Is it recorded?

Yes. Registered attendees get the recording within a week.

© Northside Code Co-op · 512 Boylston St, Boston MA
Code of Conduct · Accessibility · Sponsors

Vol. IV · No. 12 Saturday · October 4 Two Dollars · Free at the door

The Saturday Review

A quarterly of tools, methods & the small crafts of software — Northside Code Co-op
  • The Lead
  • Programme
  • Dispatches
  • Register
♦ ♦ ♦
A Workshop · Enrolment Now Open

Learning to keep receipts:
an unhurried Saturday with Git.

In a single, small-room afternoon, twenty-four newcomers will build the mental model that most self-taught programmers assemble by accident over years — and leave with a repository, a workflow, and no more folders named final v2.

Written by the Editors · Illustrated by A. Kim · Printed in Boston

Every programmer, at some point, has stared at a folder titled project-final-FINAL-use-this-one and understood, dimly, that there must be a better way. There is. It is called version control, and for thirty-odd years the working craft of software has hinged on it.

Yet Git — the version-control system that runs the world's code — is famously charmless to learn. Its documentation is terse. Its metaphors leak. Its error messages have the tone of a bureaucrat who has already decided you're wrong. Most people first meet it through panic: an interview, a new job, a class where the professor said just push it to GitHub as if that were a complete sentence.

The premise

Our premise on Saturday is simple. In five hours, taught in a small room with real coffee and a real lunch, we can hand a newcomer the model that survives contact with actual work. Not a list of commands to memorise. A picture of what Git believes about your code — snapshots on a graph, branches as movable labels, remotes as other people's copies — and then enough hands-on practice for that picture to become second nature.

The rhythm

We alternate short lessons with longer stretches of practice. You will make your first commit before the morning is out, break something before lunch, and recover from it — with a command called reflog that will feel, briefly, like a small miracle. In the afternoon, we move to GitHub, open a pull request against a real repository, and review one another's work.

The last ninety minutes are yours. Bring the folder you've been meaning to put under version control. A mentor will sit with you. By 3 PM, that project has a home on the internet, a README you wrote, and a workflow you can keep using on Monday.

Who this is for

If you have opened a terminal at least once and can save a text file, you are ready. Prior programming experience is welcome but not required. If you already know Git and simply want the afternoon lab, tell us on the form — we'll seat you accordingly.

At a Glance

DateSat, Oct 4
Time10:00 – 15:00
Where512 Boylston, Rm 304
FormatIn-person + Zoom
CostFree · lunch included
Seats24 · limited by design
PrereqsA laptop, a curiosity
"I stopped emailing myself zip files. That's the whole review." — L. Torres, Spring Cohort

Bring

LaptopMac, Windows, or Linux
ChargerOutlets are shared
A projectOptional; for the afternoon lab
II · Programme of the Day

Five hours, told plainly.

10:00
Setup & the case for version control
Install check, terminal warmup, a short history of Git and its manners.
10:30
Your first commit
init, add, commit — and what actually happened on disk.
11:30
Branching without fear
Feature branches, clean merges, the ones that go wrong, and the ones that don't.
12:30
Luncheon
Sandwiches, fruit, coffee. An unhurried break with informal Q&A.
13:15
Remotes, GitHub, pull requests
Push, pull, fork; open and review a PR against a real repository.
14:15
Bring-your-own-project lab
Ninety minutes with a mentor and the folder you've been meaning to commit.
15:00
Cheat sheet & next steps
Take-home reference, office hours, community reading list.
III · Dispatches from Prior Cohorts

Field notes.

The Recovering Hobbyist

"I finally understood what HEAD is."

Three years of Git-by-copy-paste, undone in one Saturday. She now teaches a session at her job.

The Career Switcher

"My first pull request, opened at 2:14 PM."

He arrived without ever having pushed a repository. He left with three of them and an interview lined up.

The Team Lead

"I sent my whole team the next month."

Turns out most of them had been quietly winging it. The workshop became a small internal ritual.

IV · Enrolment

Take a seat.

Twenty-four seats, given away at no cost thanks to our sponsors. A short form. A confirmation the same day. Cancellations release a spot to the waitlist — please tell us early if plans change.

Questions may be addressed to the editors at hi@northsidecodecoop.org.

Free of charge. Lunch provided. Recording available to registered attendees within one week.

Colophon · Set in Bodoni & Iowan Old Style · Printed at 512 Boylston
© MMXXVI · Northside Code Co-op

content.text:
Four self-contained mockups written to `scratch/workshop/`:

- **mock1.html** — Modern SaaS landing. Blue accent, sticky nav, hero + feature grid + hourly schedule + inline register form + FAQ. Voice: crisp, functional.
- **mock2.html** — Terminal/TTY aesthetic. Green-on-black, monospace, ASCII banner, prompts framing each section, a `git diff` "before/after brain" block, register form styled as stdin. Voice: hackerly and dry.
- **mock3.html** — Hand-drawn zine. Warm dotted paper, chunky Bodoni display, wonky rotated header with red drop-shadow, sticker chips, notebook-ruled schedule, red RSVP block. Voice: warm and playful.
- **mock4.html** — Editorial magazine ("The Saturday Review"). Bodoni masthead, two-column justified body with drop cap, sidebar of facts + pull quote, numbered sections, dispatches from prior cohorts. Voice: literary and unhurried.

Each takes a different content architecture (nav-driven / terminal prompts / zine spreads / newspaper sections), a different voice, and a different visual tone. No other files written, nothing executed.

- **mock3.html** — Hand-drawn zine. Warm dotted paper, chunky Bodoni display, wonky rotated header with red drop-shadow, sticker chips, notebook-ruled schedule, red RSVP block. Voice: warm and playful.
- **mock4.html** — Editorial magazine ("The Saturday Review"). Bodoni masthead, two-column justified body with drop cap, sidebar of facts + pull quote, numbered sections, dispatches from prior cohorts. Voice: literary and unhurried.

Each takes a different content architecture (nav-driven / terminal prompts / zine spreads / newspaper sections), a different voice, and a different visual tone. No other files written, nothing executed.
